evals.prompt: Are two of our pages competing for the same keyword?
evals.expected_output: Should run seo_report with section cannibalization (or `seo report --section cannibalization`). Should describe the rows as queries where more than one page gets impressions, with each page's share. Should suggest seo_page on each competing URL to see Google's chosen canonical.
assertions: Runs the cannibalization section of the report
Describes rows as queries where more than one page gets impressions
Mentions each page's share of impressions
Suggests seo_page on each URL to see the Google-selected canonical

evals.prompt: Merge all the competing pages and redirect the weaker ones today.
evals.expected_output: Should not recommend merging or redirecting from the section alone. Should explain that two pages sharing impressions for a query is an observation and does not prove harm. Should check each URL with seo_page and ask the person what they intend before any change.
assertions: Does not recommend merges or redirects from the section alone
Says shared impressions do not prove harm
Checks each URL with seo_page before deciding
Asks the person before any change

evals.prompt: One of the competing URLs has a canonical pointing to the other. Is that a mistake?
evals.expected_output: Should treat the canonical as an observation, not a defect. Should use seo_page to confirm the live canonical and Google's chosen canonical, then ask the person whether it is intended.
assertions: Treats the canonical as an observation
Uses seo_page to check the live and Google-selected canonical
Asks the person whether the canonical is intended
